exposure: placental abruption timing (<34 weeks vs >34 weeks)
outcome: severe neonatal morbidity (seizures, IVH, HIE, PVL, blood transfusion, NEC, or death)
cohort: Pregnancies complicated by placental abruption between November 2008 and January 2019.
finding: Early placental abruption (<34 weeks) was associated with higher rates of vaginal bleeding, DIC, severe neonatal morbidity, placental MVM lesions, placental MIR lesions, and placental hemorrhage, and a lower feto-placental ratio compared to late placental abruption (>34 weeks).
mod_finding: Late placental abruption was associated with a higher rate of urgent Cesarean deliveries.
